end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified local vegetables as having fewer food miles and being fresher.
Explained that fuel use, refrigeration and packaging can increase pollution and costs.
Compared food distances, including 80 km versus 230 km and selected 10 km as the shortest.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, tracing where food comes from, and comparing travel distances. They used the farm-to-plate method and connected longer journeys with fuel, refrigeration, packaging, pollution, and freshness. They initially needed repeated prompts for the definition, then stated it correctly later in the lesson. At home, ask Rohan to compare two foods by source, distance, freshness, and transport needs.
